input.question: What is the evolutionary purpose of having different blood types (A,B,AB,O)?
input.ground_truth: While this doesn't answer your question, it is important to understand that evolution does not have a purpose. Mutations do not happen because they can be beneficial. Random mutations happen in individuals, then over time if the mutation is beneficial and propagated via offspring, the lineage with that trait may be more fit than individuals without that trait and slowly become more predominant. A more accurate question would be "Why did organisms evolve different blood types?" I'm not trying to be pedantic for the sake of pedantry, but I think maybe this will help you understand other's answers a little more clearly.

Question: What is the evolutionary purpose of having different blood types (A,B,AB,O)?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, imagine your blood is like a team of helpers inside your body. Each helper has a special name tag—like A, B, AB, or O. Long, long ago, people got different name tags by accident, kind of like how you might get a different colored shirt from your brother or sister.

These name tags help your body fight germs and stay healthy. Sometimes, having one kind of name tag can help your body fight off some germs better, while another name tag might help with different germs. So, over a very, very long time, people with different name tags (blood types) survived better in different places and situations. That’s how we ended up with lots of different blood types in the world!

So, the different blood types are like different tools that help our bodies in different ways, and they happened by accident as people and germs changed over time.
